[[File:GermanShep1 wb.jpg|thumb|A [[German Shepherd]] is a type of dog]]

'''Dogs''' are [[mammal]]s, usually to be kept as [[pet]]s, or work on farms or for the [[police]]. Some dogs are trained to be rescue dogs and join teams such as mountain rescue.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2024-09-05|title=Dog {{!}} History, Domestication, Physical Traits, Breeds, & Facts {{!}} Britannica|url=https://www.britannica.com/animal/dog|access-date=2024-09-06|website=www.britannica.com|language=en}}</ref>
[[File:Comparison of a wolf and a pug.png|thumb|Wolves (left) were domesticated by humans into dogs (right)]]
Dogs have been bred by [[Human|humans]] from ancestral wolves. They were the first animals to live with humans.<ref>Irving-Pease, Evan K.; Ryan, Hannah; Jamieson, Alexandra; Dimopoulos, Evangelos A.; Larson, Greger; Frantz, Laurent A.F. 2018. Paleogenomics of Animal Domestication. In Lindqvist, C.; Rajora, O. (eds) ''Paleogenomics. Population Genomics''. Springer, Cham. pp. 225–272. doi:10.1007/13836_2018_55. ISBN 978-3-030-04752-8</ref> There was a lot of different types among wolves in the Late [[Pleistocene]].<ref name="Thalmann2018" /> <ref>{{Cite web|last1=Cairns|first1=Kylie M.|last2=Crowther|first2=Mathew|last3=Letnic|first3=Mike|date=2023-05-29|title=New DNA testing shatters 'wild dog' myth: most dingoes are pure|url=https://theconversation.com/new-dna-testing-shatters-wild-dog-myth-most-dingoes-are-pure-206397|access-date=2024-09-06|website=The Conversation|language=en-US}}</ref>

Today, some dogs are used as pets, and others are used to help humans do their work. They are popular pets because they are usually playful, friendly, loyal, and listen to humans. Thirty million dogs in the [[United States]] have been [[wikt:register|registered]] as [[pet]]s.<ref>{{cite book| last = Gifford| first = Clive| title = Family Flip Quiz Geography| year = 2002| publisher = Miles Kelly Publishing| isbn = 978-1-84236-146-7| author2 = Lisa Clayden }}</ref> Dogs eat both [[meat]] and [[vegetable]]s, which are often mixed together and sold in stores as [[dog food]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=CVA|first=Julie Buzby DVM, CAVCA|date=2023-12-21|title=14 Vegetables Dogs Can Eat (And May Just Love)|url=https://toegrips.com/vegetables-dogs-can-eat/|access-date=2024-09-06|website=Dr. Buzby's ToeGrips for Dogs|language=en-US}}</ref> Dogs often have jobs including police dogs, army dogs, assistance dogs, fire dogs, messenger dogs, hunting dogs, herding dogs, or rescue dogs. A baby dog is called a '''pup''' or '''puppy'''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=When Does My Puppy Finish Growing? How Long Do Puppies Grow?|url=https://www.akc.org/expert-advice/health/when-does-my-puppy-finish-growing/|access-date=2021-05-03|website=American Kennel Club|language=en}}</ref>

Dogs are sometimes known as "human's best friend" because they are kept as pets, are usually loyal, and like being around humans.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Editorial|first=Chewy|date=2018-04-05|title=Why Your Dog Is Actually Your Best Friend|url=https://be.chewy.com/dog-actually-best-friend/|access-date=2024-09-06|website=BeChewy|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Appearance and behaviour ==
Dogs can smell and hear better than humans but cannot see in full [[color]]. Due to the structure of their eyes, dogs can see better in low light than humans. They also have a larger field of vision.<ref>{{Cite web|title=How Do Dogs See the World?|url=https://www.petmd.com/dog/general-health/how-do-dogs-see-world|access-date=2024-09-06|website=www.petmd.com|language=en}}</ref>

Like wolves, wild dogs travel in groups called [[pack (canine)|packs]]. A dog in a group helps and cares for others.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RQ63-D3C9wcC&dq=domesticated+dogs+view+owner+as+alpha+male&pg=PA52|title=Domestic Cats: Their History, Breeds and Other Facts|last=Robbins|first=Nancy|date=2012-02-14|publisher=Nancy Robbins|isbn=978-1-4700-7538-5|page=52|language=en}}</ref>

== Lifespan of dogs ==
[[File:Dog and human year graph(fixed).png|thumb|This graph shows the correlation between weight and lifespan.]]
Different dog breeds have different lifespans. In general, smaller dogs live longer than bigger ones.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://news.sciencemag.org/sciencenow/2010/04/good-dogs-live-longer.html |title=Good Dogs Live Longer&nbsp;— ScienceNOW |access-date=2011-05-18 |archive-date=2011-11-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111129221514/http://news.sciencemag.org/sciencenow/2010/04/good-dogs-live-longer.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> The size and the breed of the dog change how long the dog lives on average. Breeds such as the [[Dachshund]] usually live for fifteen years, [[Chihuahua (dog)|Chihuahuas]] can reach the age of twenty. On the other hand, the [[Great Dane]] has an average lifespan of six to eight years; some Great Danes have lived for as long as ten years. An American Bulldog lives for around 15 years. Bigger dogs will have shorter lives than smaller dogs because of the pressure on its heart to move around.<ref>{{Cite web|title=50 Fascinating Facts About Dogs|url=https://www.petassure.com/new-newsletters/50-fascinating-facts-about-dogs/|access-date=2024-07-14|website=www.petassure.com}}</ref>

==Anatomy==
===Size and skeleton===
Dogs come in a wide range of sizes, from very large breeds like the [[Great Dane]] weighing 50-79 [[kilogram|kg]] and measuring 71-81 cm, to very small breeds like the [[Chihuahua]] weighing 0.5-3 kg and measuring 13-20 cm.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Byosiere|first1=Sarah-Elizabeth|last2=Chouinard|first2=Philippe A.|last3=Howell|first3=Tiffani J.|last4=Bennett|first4=Pauleen C.|date=2018-10-01|title=What do dogs (Canis familiaris) see? A review of vision in dogs and implications for cognition research|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.3758/s13423-017-1404-7|journal=Psychonomic Bulletin & Review|language=en|volume=25|issue=5|pages=1798–1813|doi=10.3758/s13423-017-1404-7|pmid=29143248 |issn=1531-5320}}</ref> There are variations in the skeletal structure among different types of dogs.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nießner|first1=Christine|last2=Denzau|first2=Susanne|last3=Malkemper|first3=Erich Pascal|last4=Gross|first4=Julia Christina|last5=Burda|first5=Hynek|last6=Winklhofer|first6=Michael|last7=Peichl|first7=Leo|date=2016-02-22|title=Cryptochrome 1 in Retinal Cone Photoreceptors Suggests a Novel Functional Role in Mammals|journal=Scientific Reports|volume=6|article-number=21848|doi=10.1038/srep21848|issn=2045-2322|pmc=4761878|pmid=26898837 |bibcode=2016NatSR...621848N }}</ref> The dog's [[skeleton]] is well-suited for running, with [[Neck (body part)|neck]] and back vertebrae having extensions for back [[Muscle|muscles]], [[rib]]s providing space for the [[heart]] and [[Lung|lungs]], and flexible shoulders.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Back pain|url=https://www.elwoodvet.net/back-pain-dogs|access-date=2025-05-08|website=Elwood vet|language=en-AU}}</ref> Selective breeding over time has led to larger [[skeleton]]s in breeds like smaller skeletons in breeds like [[terrier]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Miller|first1=Paul E.|last2=Murphy|first2=Christopher J.|date=1995-12-15|title=Vision in dogs|url=https://avmajournals.avma.org/view/journals/javma/207/12/javma.1995.207.12.1623.xml|journal=Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association|language=EN|volume=207|issue=12|pages=1623–1634|doi=10.2460/javma.1995.207.12.1623 |pmid=7493905 }}</ref> Most dogs have 26 [[vertebrae]] in their [[Tail|tails]], but some naturally have as few as three. The dog's [[skull]] has consistent components across breeds but varies in shape.<ref name="The Dog Encyclopedia: The Definitive Visual Guide - DK - Google Books">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cBGmEAAAQBAJ&q=Dog|title=The Dog Encyclopedia: The Definitive Visual Guide|last=DK|date=2023-07-06|publisher=Dorling Kindersley Limited|isbn=978-0-241-63310-6|language=en}}</ref>

=== Senses ===
[[File:Vision comparison with dogs.jpg|thumb|The left half shows how dogs see compared to humans.]]

Dogs have senses like [[sight]], [[hearing]], [[Sense of smell|smell]], [[taste]], [[touch]], and sensing [[Earth's magnetic field|Earth's magnetic fields]]. Studies show they may detect small changes in magnetism and prefer to poop facing [[north]] or [[south]] when the magnetic field is calm.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Nießner |first1=Christine |last2=Denzau |first2=Susanne |last3=Malkemper |first3=Erich Pascal |author-link3=Erich Pascal Malkemper |last4=Gross |first4=Julia Christina |last5=Burda |first5=Hynek |last6=Winklhofer |first6=Michael |last7=Peichl |first7=Leo |year=2016 |title=Cryptochrome 1 in Retinal Cone Photoreceptors Suggests a Novel Functional Role in Mammals |journal=Scientific Reports |volume=6 |article-number=21848 |bibcode=2016NatSR...621848N |doi=10.1038/srep21848 |pmc=4761878 |pmid=26898837}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hart |first1=Vlastimil |last2=Nováková |first2=Petra |last3=Malkemper |first3=Erich Pascal |last4=Begall |first4=Sabine |last5=Hanzal |first5=Vladimír |last6=Ježek |first6=Miloš |last7=Kušta |first7=Tomáš |last8=Němcová |first8=Veronika |last9=Adámková |first9=Jana |last10=Benediktová |first10=Kateřina |last11=Červený |first11=Jaroslav |last12=Burda |first12=Hynek |title=Dogs are sensitive to small variations of the Earth's magnetic field |journal=Frontiers in Zoology |date=December 2013 |volume=10 |issue=1 |page=80 |doi=10.1186/1742-9994-10-80 |doi-access=free |pmc=3882779 |pmid=24370002 }}</ref>

Dogs see mainly yellows, blues, and grays. They cannot see red and green because they have fewer color-detecting cells than humans.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Byosiere |first1=Sarah-Elizabeth |last2=Chouinard |first2=Philippe A. |last3=Howell |first3=Tiffani J. |last4=Bennett |first4=Pauleen C. |date=1 October 2018 |title=What do dogs (Canis familiaris) see? A review of vision in dogs and implications for cognition research |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.3758/s13423-017-1404-7 |journal=Psychonomic Bulletin & Review |language=en |volume=25 |issue=5 |pages=1798–1813 |doi=10.3758/s13423-017-1404-7 |pmid=29143248 |issn=1531-5320}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Siniscalchi |first1=Marcello |last2=d'Ingeo |first2=Serenella |last3=Fornelli |first3=Serena |last4=Quaranta |first4=Angelo |date=8 November 2017 |title=Are dogs red–green colour blind? |journal=Royal Society Open Science |volume=4 |issue=11 |article-number=170869 |doi=10.1098/rsos.170869 |doi-access=free |issn=2054-5703 |pmc=5717654 |pmid=29291080 |bibcode=2017RSOS....470869S }}</ref> Their eyes are less sharp than humans', seeing details up to eight times worse.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Pongrácz |first1=Péter |last2=Ujvári |first2=Vera |last3=Faragó |first3=Tamás |last4=Miklósi |first4=Ádám |last5=Péter |first5=András |date=1 July 2017 |title=Do you see what I see? The difference between dog and human visual perception may affect the outcome of experiments |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0376635716303400 |journal=Behavioural Processes |volume=140 |pages=53–60 |doi=10.1016/j.beproc.2017.04.002 |pmid=28396145 |issn=0376-6357}}</ref>

Smell is their strongest sense. Dogs have 40 times more [[Sense_of_smell#Olfactory_reception_cells|smell receptor]]s than humans—up to 300 million in breeds like [[bloodhound]]s.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Coren |first=Stanley |url=https://archive.org/details/howdogsthinkunde00core |title=How dogs think: understanding the canine mind |date=2004 |publisher=New York : Free Press |others=Internet Archive |isbn=978-0-7432-2232-7 |pages=50–81}}</ref> They hear sounds four times farther than humans (up to 400 meters).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Barber |first1=Anjuli L. A. |last2=Wilkinson |first2=Anna |last3=Montealegre-Z |first3=Fernando |last4=Ratcliffe |first4=Victoria F. |last5=Guo |first5=Kun |last6=Mills |first6=Daniel S. |year=2020 |title=A comparison of hearing and auditory functioning between dogs and humans |url=http://comparative-cognition-and-behavior-reviews.org/vol15_barber_wilkinson_montealegre-z_ratcliffe_guo_mills/ |journal=Comparative Cognition & Behavior Reviews |volume=15 |pages=45–94 |doi=10.3819/CCBR.2020.150007|doi-access=free }}</ref>

Whiskers help dogs sense vibrations, air movements, and nearby objects in the dark. They also help guide food to the mouth.<ref>{{Cite news |date=24 June 2015 |title=Dog Senses - A Dog's Sense of Touch Compared to Humans {{!}} Puppy And Dog Care |work=Puppy And Dog Care |url=http://blog.puppyanddogcare.com/dog-senses-touch/ |access-date=18 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150624013803/http://blog.puppyanddogcare.com/dog-senses-touch/ |archive-date=24 June 2015 | vauthors = Care PA }}</ref>

== Dogs and humans ==
Dogs are often called "man's best [[friend]]" because they fit in with human life. Dogs can serve people in many ways. For example, there are [[guard dog]]s, [[hunting dog]]s, [[Sheepdog|herding dogs]], [[guide dog]]s for [[blind]] people, and [[police dog]]s. There are also dogs that are trained to smell for diseases in the human body or to find bombs or [[illegal drugs]]. These dogs sometimes help police in airports or other areas. Sniffer dogs (usually [[beagle]]s) are sometimes trained for this job. Dogs have even been sent by [[Russia]]ns into [[outer space]], a few years before any human being. The first dog sent up was named [[Laika]], but she died within a few hours.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2023-10-08|title=Why Are Dogs Man's Best Friend? The Unbreakable Bond Explained - Vet Advises|url=https://vetadvises.com/why-are-dogs-mans-best-friend/|access-date=2024-07-14|language=en-US}}</ref>

There is much more variety in dogs than in cats. This is mainly because humans have selected and bred dogs for specific jobs and functions.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Why are there so many dog breeds but only a few cat breeds?|url=https://cordis.europa.eu/article/id/442154-why-are-there-so-many-dog-breeds-but-only-a-few-cat-breeds|access-date=2024-09-06|website=CORDIS {{!}} European Commission|language=en}}</ref>

== Dog breeds ==
[[File:Big and little dog 1.jpg|thumb|200px|Dogs are bred into very different breeds: here a [[Great Dane]] and a small [[Chihuahua (dog)|Chihuahua]].]]
:''See main article, [[List of dog breeds]].''
There are over 450 recognized dog [[breed]]s, according to the [[American Kennel Club]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.akc.org/press-center/articles-resources/facts-and-stats/becoming-recognized/|title=Becoming Recognized by the AKC|publisher=AKC.org|accessdate=July 21, 2025}}</ref> Dogs started to become more diverse during the [[Victorian era]] when humans began controlling which dogs were bred.<ref name="The Dog Encyclopedia: The Definitive Visual Guide - DK - Google Books" /> Most breeds come from a small number of original dogs from the last 200 years. Since then, dogs have changed quickly in appearance and have been selectively bred by people.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Pendleton|first1=Amanda L.|last2=Shen|first2=Feichen|last3=Taravella|first3=Angela M.|last4=Emery|first4=Sarah|last5=Veeramah|first5=Krishna R.|last6=Boyko|first6=Adam R.|last7=Kidd|first7=Jeffrey M.|date=2018-06-28|title=Comparison of village dog and wolf genomes highlights the role of the neural crest in dog domestication|journal=BMC Biology|volume=16|issue=1|pages=64|doi=10.1186/s12915-018-0535-2|doi-access=free |issn=1741-7007|pmc=6022502|pmid=29950181}}</ref> These breeds have unique features like body size, skull shape, tail type, [[fur]] texture, and color.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2025-03-27|title=Chihuahua dog {{!}} Size, Lifespan, Barking, Personality & Origin {{!}} Britannica|url=https://www.britannica.com/animal/Chihuahua-dog|access-date=2025-05-08|website=www.britannica.com|language=en}}</ref> Humans have bred dogs for specific traits to help with tasks such as guarding, herding, hunting, retrieving, and scent detection. Dogs also show different behaviors like being very social, boldness, and aggression.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2025-05-02|title=Great Dane {{!}} Size, Lifespan, Temperament & Health Issues {{!}} Britannica|url=https://www.britannica.com/animal/Great-Dane|access-date=2025-05-08|website=www.britannica.com|language=en}}</ref> Today, dogs are found all over the world.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Parker |first1=Heidi G. |last2=Dreger |first2=Dayna L. |last3=Rimbault |first3=Maud |last4=Davis |first4=Brian W. |last5=Mullen |first5=Alexandra B. |last6=Carpintero-Ramirez |first6=Gretchen |last7=Ostrander |first7=Elaine A. |title=Genomic Analyses Reveal the Influence of Geographic Origin, Migration, and Hybridization on Modern Dog Breed Development |journal=[[Cell Reports]] |year=2017 |volume=19 |issue=4 |pages=697–708 |doi=10.1016/j.celrep.2017.03.079 |pmid=28445722 |pmc=5492993 |bibcode=2017CellR..19..697P |doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Health ==
Dogs can get many different diseases. Some are born with these problems ([[birth defect]]) and others get sick as they get older.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Congenital and Inherited Disorders Affecting Multiple Body Systems of Dogs - Dog Owners|url=https://www.merckvetmanual.com/dog-owners/disorders-affecting-multiple-body-systems-of-dogs/congenital-and-inherited-disorders-affecting-multiple-body-systems-of-dogs|access-date=2026-01-13|website=Merck Veterinary Manual|language=en-US}}</ref> [[Neoplasm|Neoplasia]] is the most common cause of death for dogs.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Paul|first1=Dr Mike|last2=DVM|title=Neoplasia in Dogs|url=https://www.pethealthnetwork.com/dog-health/dog-diseases-conditions-a-z/neoplasia-dogs|access-date=2026-01-13|website=Pet Health Network|language=en}}</ref> There are other common causes of [[death]] for dogs like [[Heart failure|heart]] and [[renal failure]].
